meta.title: Devlog: October 11, 2026 - October 18, 2026
meta.description: released traybridge and stoplight updates while expanding local media-production workflows and continuing due or die optimization.

bullets.text: optimization work across the app, configuration, and test coverage is still in progress.

summary.text: i spent some time tightening up due or die this week. it is still a work in progress, but the optimization pass is moving along.

bullets.text: launched the initial cutroom workspace for reviewing existing footage and assembling local portrait videos with source audio.
added optional local caption-removal previews so editors can review repairs before approving a clip.
expanded the studio to support photo slideshows alongside video-based edits.
added product-context and hashtag research suggestions that remain reviewable before becoming approved settings.
documented installation, design standards, and validation guidance for using the workspace on another windows device.

summary.text: i got the core of cutroom into place this week. the goal is a calmer local workspace for turning existing media into edits, with a few more useful review steps before anything gets published.

bullets.text: created an initial set of draft benchmark assemblies built from approved hook and product-demo clips.

summary.text: i also put together some early benchmark edits to pressure-test the assembly workflow. they are drafts for now, which is exactly where experiments should be.

bullets.text: released stoplight 0.1.1 with clearer tray and dashboard states for completed unread chats, chats awaiting input, and chats still running.
improved recovery of saved chat status so completed replies and pending input are represented more reliably after reconnecting.
documented how stoplight can pair with traybridge to keep chat status visible on additional displays.

summary.text: i wanted stoplight to answer the more useful question at a glance: what finished, what needs me, and what is still going. this release makes those states a lot easier to read.

bullets.text: released the traybridge 0.1.5 preview with portable downloads and a walkthrough for setting up native notification areas on additional displays.
added stronger release, recovery, and cleanup safeguards to make setup and removal more dependable.
clarified supported windows requirements and added guidance for security reports and ongoing compatibility review.

summary.text: i shipped an early traybridge preview this week. it is intentionally narrow in supported scope, but the release path and recovery work now have much more of the necessary guardrail energy.
